sections.skill: Find the best value under stated constraints and show nothing better is possible

questions.prompt: Two whole numbers add up to 20. What is the largest possible product?
A rectangular pen uses exactly 24 meters of fence, and its sides are whole numbers of meters. What is the largest possible area, in square meters?
A 12-hour digital clock shows times from 1:00 to 12:59. Which time has the largest product of its digits?
Using coins worth 1, 5, 10 and 25 cents, the fewest coins that make exactly 30 cents is 2.
Whole numbers x and y are each 0 or more, with x + 2y at most 10 and x at most 6. Make x + 3y as large as possible. Give x and y.
questions.rule: (x == 0 and y == 5) and isInteger(x) and x >= 0 and isInteger(y) and y >= 0
questions.correct_answer: any values that satisfy: (x == 0 and y == 5) and isInteger(x) and x >= 0 and isInteger(y) and y >= 0 (example: x = 0, y = 5)

sections.skill: Strategy: find a good answer, then prove nothing beats it
sections.relationship: Students stop at the first good answer. A best-answer problem needs two parts: an example that reaches a value, and a reason no answer can do better.
sections.author_note: Students stop at the first good answer. A best-answer problem needs two parts: an example that reaches a value, and a reason no answer can do better.

lesson.title: Find a good answer, then prove nothing beats it
text: Try several cases in an organized way and keep the best so far.
Look for a limit (a bound): a reason every answer is at most some value.
If your best example reaches the bound, it is the best possible.

example.title: Worked example (a different problem)
prompt: Two whole numbers add to 9. What is the largest product?
steps: Moving away from the middle makes the product smaller, so 20 is the largest.

questions.prompt: Two whole numbers add to 14. What is the largest possible product?
To show that a value is the largest possible, it is enough to find one example that reaches it.
Which numbers from the list 4, 9, 2, 7, 5 give the largest sum if you may choose any two?
Using coins worth 1, 5 and 10 cents, what is the fewest coins that make 27 cents?
A rectangle with whole-number sides and perimeter 20 can have area 25.

sections.skill: When the obvious choice is not best
sections.relationship: Harder: greedy choices that fail, and products.
sections.label: ADVANCED APPLICATION

questions.prompt: Coins are worth 1, 4 and 6 cents. What is the fewest coins that make exactly 8 cents?
Whole numbers add up to 10 (you choose how many numbers). What is the largest possible product?
Coins are worth 1, 4 and 6 cents. Always taking the largest coin that fits gives the fewest coins for every amount.
A backpack can hold at most 10 kilograms. Items: tent 6 kg, value 8; stove 4 kg, value 5; food 5 kg, value 6; lamp 1 kg, value 3. Which choice has the greatest total value?
Two whole numbers are each at least 1 and their product is 36. Make their sum as small as possible. Give the two numbers.
questions.rule: (a == 6 and b == 6) and isInteger(a) and a >= 0 and isInteger(b) and b >= 0
questions.correct_answer: any values that satisfy: (a == 6 and b == 6) and isInteger(a) and a >= 0 and isInteger(b) and b >= 0 (example: a = 6, b = 6)

sections.relationship: Expert: bounds that match the best example.
sections.label: EXPERT CHALLENGE

questions.prompt: Whole numbers add up to 20 (you choose how many numbers). What is the largest possible product?
Coins are worth 1, 7 and 10 cents. What is the fewest coins that make exactly 14 cents?
Among rectangles with whole-number sides and area 36, the 6 by 6 square has the smallest perimeter.
Whole numbers a, b and c are each at least 1 and add up to 12. Make the product a x b x c as large as possible. Give a, b and c.
questions.rule: (a == 4 and b == 4 and c == 4) and isInteger(a) and a >= 0 and isInteger(b) and b >= 0 and isInteger(c) and c >= 0
questions.correct_answer: any values that satisfy: (a == 4 and b == 4 and c == 4) and isInteger(a) and a >= 0 and isInteger(b) and b >= 0 and isInteger(c) and c >= 0 (example: a = 4, b = 4, c = 4)
